doc.title: Mrs. P. Thomas Agnes Brown Interview, 1960-10-12

title: Vista Garden dance advertisement and its musicians
summary: An ad for dancing at Vista Garden near Cottage Grove touts each band member's specialty; Roy Kramer made records.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Let's see. Dancers. There is a reason. Tom Brown is back in town, and if you have never danced to Tom Brown's dance music, then you have never danced. If you want to be thrilled again with that intoxicating dance music, don't miss visiting the Vista Garden, 47th Street, near Cottage Grove Avenue, every Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday, matinee, and night. The orchestra. Tom Brown himself, the originator of the jazz craze. Abe Friedman plays the piano and is well-known with his music studio. Roy Kramer, clarinet, known for his weird harmony. Joe Gallagher. Gallagher. G-A-L-A-I-G-U-R-I. I don't know how to pronounce that. Known for the laughing cornet.
Paul Crawford, how'd you say? Gallagher.

Gallagher. Oh, Charlie Hawk plays southern harmony on his old banjo. George Lee plays the some-leading saxophone. No, I'm sorry. George Lee plays some-leading saxophone. Ted Brown bass, known for his picking novelty. Earl Carter drums, known as the Tempo Kid. I thank you. That's nice.
And you've got who was in the band. Roy Kramer made some records. Yes. I've heard of him, too. And, of course, naturally, I've heard of Ted and Tom.
